clue.text: Looking a little worse for wear betrays drunk

definitions.text: Looking a little worse for wear

parts.note: to shop someone is slang for informing on them to the police
oiled is informal for tipsy

explanation.surface: Someone looks rough and gives away that they have been drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Betrays' looks like the link to the definition, but it is the first half of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Shop-soiled goods are slightly damaged or faded from being on display in a store.

clue.text: Romantic revival back home? No, on holiday finally taken abroad

parts.note: to second a proposal is to back it

indicators.note: something taken abroad is moved away from its usual place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the final letter of holiday

explanation.surface: A couple weigh up whether to rekindle their romance at home or abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reads as part of 'back home' but is a verb meaning support on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A second honeymoon is a holiday taken by a long-married couple to revive the romance of their marriage.

clue.text: Being pulled along over to start of waterway

parts.note: onto means over to a new position or topic

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of waterway

explanation.surface: A barge is hauled across to the beginning of a canal.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle or boat on tow is attached by a rope and dragged along by another.

clue.text: Chief, first to size up British Army corps

indicators.note: first to a word means its opening letter is the one taken

parts.note: the opening letter of size
taken as written
the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: A commander is the first to assess a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme means highest in rank or authority, like a chief or principal figure.

clue.text: Dines out with couple at wits' end

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of order and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
a couple is a pair

explanation.surface: A frazzled diner goes out to eat with another couple.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at your wits' end means having no hope left about what to do, which is despair.

clue.text: Forward almost blowing top

indicators.note: blowing its top means the word loses its uppermost letter, which in a down answer is the first

parts.note: nearly is a synonym of almost

explanation.surface: Something lurches ahead, nearly losing its lid.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the top of a word is its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward can mean ahead of time, as in a forward spring, which is an early one.

clue.text: Intrepid person crossing lake

indicators.note: a person crossing something spans it, so the word for person goes around the other piece

parts.note: bod is informal British slang for a person
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A fearless individual walks across a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrepid and bold both describe someone brave and undaunted by danger.

clue.text: Her co-star upset big band

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A singer's co-star is annoyed with the big band backing them.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a large ensemble of musicians, so a big band in the literal sense.

clue.text: What some beetles spread, this male deduces, sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong and been thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man works out, with regret, which illness certain beetles carry.
explanation.definitionFit: This fungal tree infection is carried from tree to tree by elm bark beetles.

clue.text: Banger and firecracker ultimately causing a hole in the ground

parts.note: a banger and a crate are both slang for an old, run-down car

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so the closing letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the final letter of firecracker

explanation.surface: Sausage-shaped fireworks blow a pit in the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banger' plants the idea of a firework, but here it is British slang for a battered old car.
explanation.definitionFit: A crater is a bowl-shaped pit made in the ground, for instance by an explosion.

clue.text: Extremely upset — extremely upset suffering setback in competition

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the next word

parts.note: a cup is a competition, such as the FA Cup

indicators.note: a setback sends something backwards, so the selected letters run in reverse
extremely, read literally, means taking the letters at the extremes of the word

parts.note: the outer letters of upset

explanation.surface: A competitor is devastated after a reverse in a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The same two words appear twice: first as the definition, then as wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut up is an informal idiom for being very distressed or hurt.

clue.text: Daughter lost red torch in European port

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

indicators.note: something lost is in disarray and out of place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl mislaid her red torch while visiting a Continental harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Dordrecht is a river port city in the Netherlands, south-east of Rotterdam.

clue.text: Reformed island state

parts.note: something reformed is made new
Jersey is a Channel Island

explanation.surface: An island territory that has been reorganised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformed' looks like an anagram signal, but it supplies a word of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: New Jersey is one of the fifty United States, named after the Channel Island.

clue.text: The most violent part of state (Ethiopia)

indicators.note: of here means made from, so the letters come from within the words that follow

parts.note: found running across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A news item about the bloodiest region of an Ethiopian state.
explanation.definitionFit: In the teeth of a gale means in its fiercest part, so teeth is the most violent part.

clue.text: A legend enthrals — possibly this fairy tale

indicators.note: possibly hints that the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A captivating legend might well be this famous children's story.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grimm brothers' tale of two siblings and a witch's gingerbread house is among the best-known fairy stories.

clue.text: Mean boy in a Yorkshire town

parts.note: the norm is the average or mean
Anton is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A nasty lad lives in a northern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' poses as an adjective for unkind; it is the noun for an average.
explanation.definitionFit: Normanton is a market town in West Yorkshire, near Wakefield.

clue.text: Doctor providing answer in a Yorkshire town

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
providing and if both introduce a condition
to field a question is to answer it

explanation.surface: A GP provides answers to patients in a northern English town.
explanation.definitionFit: Driffield is a market town in the East Riding of Yorkshire.

clue.text: Former PM attending dinner earl prepared in part of the UK

parts.note: Lord North was British Prime Minister from 1770 to 1782

indicators.note: something prepared has been made up or worked into shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An ex-premier goes to a dinner an aristocrat has laid on in one of the home nations.
explanation.definitionFit: Northern Ireland is one of the four countries making up the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Watch woodsman

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pocket watch with a hinged cover protecting the glass
second meaning: someone who tracks game in the forest

explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' looks like a verb telling you to observe the woodsman; it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a type of covered pocket timepiece and a person who stalks animals, as in the woodsman of folk tales.

clue.text: Letter in English, heartlessly short, put in stack

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: put in places the preceding letters inside the word that follows

parts.note: a pile is a stack

indicators.note: without its heart a word loses its middle, leaving just its two ends

parts.note: the outer letters of short

explanation.surface: An English letter, curt and unkind, is placed on a heap of mail.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a letter, especially a formal one like those in the New Testament.

clue.text: Long period of time close to Ramadan

parts.note: a year is a period of time

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter of Ramadan

explanation.surface: A lengthy stretch of time near the month of fasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' reads as an adjective with period; it is the verb meaning to crave.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something and to yearn for it both mean to desire it intensely.

clue.text: Bob Hope film has old film comic in fits

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: in places the jumbled word inside the one that follows

parts.note: taken as written, as the outer piece

indicators.note: comic suggests treating the word for laughs and mangling it, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A Bob Hope movie features a vintage film comedian in hysterics.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters go after the first letter of the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Off Limits is a 1953 comedy film starring Bob Hope as a boxing manager.

clue.text: Bracing air round region

parts.note: O is round in shape
a zone is a region

explanation.surface: Fresh, invigorating air surrounds an area.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is informal, especially British, for the fresh, invigorating air of the seaside.

clue.text: Unsuitable home, small apartment

parts.note: being in means being at home
apt is the abbreviation for apartment

explanation.surface: A tiny flat makes an inappropriate place to live.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means not appropriate or not fitting the purpose.

clue.text: To win one must employ honest manoeuvring

indicators.note: manoeuvring means moving things around into new positions, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice that success requires fair play and clever tactics.
explanation.definitionFit: In horse racing a bet placed on the nose is a bet for the horse to win outright.

clue.text: Item of jewellery one found amongst Scarlett's property?

indicators.note: found amongst means sitting inside, so the first piece goes within the second

parts.note: Tara is Scarlett O'Hara's plantation in Gone with the Wind
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A piece of jewellery discovered among Scarlett's possessions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Property' suggests belongings, but it is the estate itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental headband worn by women on formal occasions.

clue.text: Girl in Fun in Acapulco

indicators.note: in tells you the letters sit inside the words around it

parts.note: found running across the three words

explanation.surface: A young woman features in the Elvis film Fun in Acapulco.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is a link; the second is the hiding signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nina is a girl's name, used here as an example of the category girl.

clue.text: Nervously attended the Parisian plant

indicators.note: nervously suggests twitching and jittering, so the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An anxious visitor went to a plant show in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead-nettle is a wild flower that looks like a nettle but has no sting.
